cards.text: The LORD is still answering Job out of the whirlwind, and friend, Job is NOT the one asking the questions anymore. Now the LORD turns to the wild animals, starting with a lioness and young lions crouched in their dens, lying in wait in the thicket.

cards.question: Those young lions are crouched in their dens, lying in wait. What does the LORD ask Job about them?

answers.text: Can you hunt the prey for them
Can you teach them how to roar
Can you count how many there are

cards.text: From the lions, the LORD goes to a bird: the raven. Its young ones are wandering around with nothing to eat.

cards.question: When the young ravens wander around with nothing to eat, they cry out to ___.
The LORD asks Job who provides food for the raven. What's the point of a question like that?

answers.text: God is the one who feeds them
Job was supposed to feed them

cards.text: Next the LORD asks if Job knows when mountain goats and deer give birth, or how many months they carry their young. Friend, I can barely time a batch of cookies, and I've got a TIMER.
They crouch down and deliver their young. And those little ones thrive and grow up out in the open field.

cards.question: The young goats and fawns grow up out in the open field. Once they're grown, what do they do?

answers.text: They leave and do not return
They stay close to their mothers

cards.text: Then comes the wild donkey, and the LORD asks who set him free from the harness. Friend, that donkey's got the kind of freedom I used to dream about in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The wild donkey runs free with no harness. Where does the LORD say He made the donkey's home?
The wild donkey loves the noise of the city and listens for the shouts of a driver.

cards.text: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing. Next on the LORD's list: the wild ox.

cards.question: The LORD asks Job if the wild ox will serve him, stay by his manger at night and plow his valleys. What answer is the LORD pointing to?

answers.text: No one can make him do that
Yes if Job feeds him first

cards.question: The LORD asks if Job can rely on the wild ox's great ___ and leave his hard work to him.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks if Job can trust the wild ox to bring in his grain and gather it to the threshing floor. Friend, I wouldn't trust that ox to carry ONE cookie box across my bakery.
Now the LORD gets to the ostrich, whose wings flap joyfully but can't match the stork's pinions and feathers. And she leaves her eggs on the ground to warm in the sand.

cards.question: The ostrich remembers that a foot or a wild animal could crush the eggs she left on the ground.
The ostrich treats her young harshly, as if they aren't hers. The LORD says God has deprived her of ___.

cards.text: But don't count the ostrich out. When she proudly spreads her wings, she finds something to laugh at.

cards.question: When the ostrich proudly spreads her wings, who does she laugh at?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks if Job gave the horse his strength and his mane. Friend, I've got the biggest mustache in the Dorinverse, and even I'm not handing any of it out.
This horse leaps like a locust and snorts proudly. He paws in the valley, rejoices in his strength and charges into battle.

cards.question: The war horse charges into battle. How does he face fear?

cards.text: A quiver rattles at his side, spears flash, and he's trembling with excitement. Friend, I tremble too, but only when the oven timer goes off and I'm all the way across the bakery.

cards.question: The war horse cannot stand still when the ___ sounds.
The war horse catches the scent of battle from far away.

cards.text: Then the LORD looks up at the sky. There's the hawk spreading his wings toward the south, and the eagle soaring up high to make his nest.

cards.question: The LORD asks if the hawk flies by Job's understanding and the eagle soars at Job's command. What answer is He pointing to?

answers.text: Job has nothing to do with it
Job taught them both to fly
They fly only when Job calls

cards.text: From his stronghold on a rocky crag, the eagle spies out food from far away. And where the slain are, there he is.

cards.question: Then the LORD speaks to Job again. What does He say the one who argues with God should do?

cards.text: Now it's Job's turn to answer the LORD. This is a man who has had a LOT to say for a LOT of chapters.

cards.question: Job answers the LORD at last. What does Job call himself?
Job asks how he could ever reply to the LORD. What does Job do with his hand?

answers.text: He places it over his mouth
He lifts it up toward heaven
He covers his eyes with it

cards.question: Job tells the LORD he has spoken once and then twice, and he still has more to add.

cards.text: And right there, Job goes quiet. But stick around, friend, because this conversation isn't over.

findings.problem: The card says the LORD is answering Job out of the whirlwind. That fact comes from Job 38:1, which is outside the passage, but the card cites only Job 38:39-40 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The right answer "No one can make him do that" widens the LORD's questions to everyone. In Job 39:9-10 the LORD asks only whether Job can make the wild ox serve him.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Multiple choice is 5 of the 8 choice cards. Fill in the blank has 2 and true or false has 1, so one type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "feathers" is a near-match. Job 39:13 says the ostrich's wings cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork, so a baker could argue she lacks feathers.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "Then the LORD looks up at the sky" says the LORD did something the text never says. The storyteller line adds a fact.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: No card tells the LORD's challenge in Job 40:2, "Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty?" That line is the heart of the LORD's closing word and is what Job answers. The walkthrough jumps from the eagle straight to a question about giving an answer, with no story card to set up the turn.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Multiple choice is 6 of the 11 choice cards. True or false has 3 and fill in the blank has 2, so one type dominates the stop by a wide margin. Both stops also lean on multiple choice in the same way.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
